F-23_CRIT_security.problem: C8 SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS requires an exact <=200-char excerpt, so hardcoded_secret / secret_in_url / weak_credential findings copy real credential values verbatim into norm artifacts AND into paid-LLM context, then feed R11 security synthesis. H1's redaction rule existed only inside the 'Legacy Context (for intent only; never as evidence)' block -- explicitly non-binding, and run_extraction_v4.py:104-110 confirms the runtime injects no block by that name, so it was inert.
fix: PROMPTSET_RULES.md: new top-level '## Secret Redaction Rules' section, marked BINDING, that explicitly OVERRIDES the exact-excerpt Evidence Rule where they conflict; names the concrete <REDACTED> masking token; gives 5 worked transforms (AWS/OpenAI/Bearer-JWT/webhook-URL/PEM); defines the secret-span vocabulary; states 'when in doubt, redact'; and forbids over-redaction of key NAMES/paths.
Evidence Rules amended so the exact-excerpt clause points at the redaction carve-out rather than silently contradicting it.

PROMPT_C8: new '#### SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS -- Hard Requirement: redact every secret value (BINDING)' in the binding body + a redacted worked example + procedure step 5 now mandates masking on capture.

PROMPT_H1: redaction promoted OUT of Legacy Context into a binding '### Hard Requirement -- never emit a secret value (BINDING)'; Goal restated as names/paths/locations-not-values; procedure step 2 mandates masking on capture.
PROMPT_H7: new binding Hard Requirement (schema metadata only; no row contents/values).
PROMPT_M3/M4/M5 safe-exports: procedure step 4 upgraded from the vague 'redact if found' to a BINDING key-names-only + <REDACTED> masking rule.
F-23_CRIT_security.why_it_reaches_the_model: All six prompts carry '## Shared Rules' pointing at PROMPTSET_RULES.md, and run_extraction_v5._inject_promptset_rules() appends that file to any such prompt before dispatch. test_binding_rules_reach_the_model_via_runtime_injection asserts the rendered prompt for each of the six actually contains the redaction section and the worked example -- i.e. the rule is proven present in the payload, not merely present in a file.

F-31_HIGH.problem: promptset.yaml declares required_prompt_sections but had ZERO runtime readers (maintainers' own comment at run_extraction_v4.py:104-110 documented this as a known gap left as-is). A section validator existed at lib/promptgen/template_renderer.py:20-37,208-251 wired to nothing. A prompt could lose its Anti-Fabrication Rules and still be dispatched to a paid model.
fix: template_renderer.validate_rendered_prompt() now accepts required_sections (so the promptset manifest is the single source of truth) and honors the '## Shared Rules' pointer for the 4 shared boilerplate sections -- matching the offline linter's existing semantics (scripts/repo_truth_extractor_promptset_audit_v4.py) so runtime and lint agree instead of contradicting.

run_extraction_v4.py: new validate_promptset_sections() + PromptSectionContractError; load_promptset() now enforces the contract and FAILS CLOSED. The resigned 'known gap left as-is' comment is replaced by the enforcement it described as missing. An enforce_sections=False escape hatch is retained for tooling that must inspect a broken promptset.

run_extraction_v5.py async R dispatch (~line 20196): ADDED the missing _inject_promptset_rules() call. NEWLY DISCOVERED THIS PACKET, not in the audit text: only the sync dispatch site (run_step, ~13456) injected. Every prompt submitted through the async R batch seam reached the model with its Shared Rules pointer UNRESOLVED -- meaning the whole anti-fab regime, and now the F-23 redaction rule, never arrived on that path. Both sites are now pinned by test at exactly 2 calls.
F-31_HIGH.empirical_result: The shipped v4 promptset passes its own contract: 0 issues across all 136 declared prompts. Enforcement is therefore live, not aspirational, and does not block any real run.

F-27_H_M_part_and_F-33_MED.problem: Gen-1 'Legacy Context' JSON container shapes in the A- and H-phase prompts mandated generated_at, directly contradicting the binding Determinism Rules ('Norm outputs MUST NOT contain: generated_at, timestamp, created_at, updated_at, run_id'). For several H steps the legacy shape was the ONLY field-level spec available, so the contradicting spec was the more concrete of the two.
F-27_H_M_part_and_F-33_MED.fix: Stripped 21 determinism-violating key lines across 17 prompts (A2-A9, H0-H7, H9). Every removal was verified to lie INSIDE a Legacy Context block before editing; the script refused to touch any binding-body occurrence and reported none. M-phase had zero occurrences (checked, not assumed).
F-27_H_M_part_and_F-33_MED.scope_note: The T-phase share of F-27 (TP_BACKLOG_TOPN) is owned by TP-RTE-TRUTH-R3-005c and was deliberately NOT touched; the new regression test excludes PROMPT_T* for exactly this reason so it cannot fail on another packet's unlanded work.

F-08_LOW.problem: Three contract-map guards called pytest.skip() when their target artifact was absent from the compiled contract map -- reporting green while checking nothing if the target stopped being emitted.
F-08_LOW.fix: test_tp_rtx_v5_phase_recovery_hardening.py:327,381,397 -> pytest.fail() with a message distinguishing 'regression this guard exists to catch' from 'test targets a stale artifact name'.
F-08_LOW.empirical_result: 23 passed / 0 skipped after the change -- the targets DO currently emit, so this closes a latent hole rather than papering over a live one.

not_live_verified_ledger: REDACTION EFFECTIVENESS IS NOT PROVEN. This packet proves the redaction rule is (a) written, (b) BINDING rather than marooned in a non-binding Legacy Context block, (c) explicitly overriding the conflicting exact-excerpt Evidence Rule, and (d) empirically present in the assembled prompt payload for all six secret-touching steps. It does NOT prove any live model obeys it. That requires live evals with seeded fake secrets and is out of this packet's dry-run mandate.
No live extraction run was performed; no artifact produced by a real model was inspected for leaked secrets.
The section validator is proven to fail closed on a synthetic broken promptset and to pass the real one. It has not been observed rejecting a real regression in a live run.

The async-R injection fix is proven by source-level call-site pinning + the sync path's existing injection tests. The async batch seam itself was not exercised end-to-end (needs live provider batch submission).
F-27's T-phase share and F-33's wider Gen-1 container-shape reconciliation beyond generated_at/run_id are NOT addressed here (owned by R3-005c / R3-005d respectively).

residual_risks.risk: Prompt-level redaction is an INSTRUCTION, not an ENFORCEMENT. A model that ignores the rule still emits the secret, and nothing downstream re-scans SECRETS_RISK_LOCATIONS.json for unredacted values before it is written or before it feeds R11.
residual_risks.recommendation: Follow-up packet: apply output_safety.sanitize_payload_for_output() (or lib/truth_labels._safe_scalar, which already has _SECRET_SHAPED_RE + _HIGH_ENTROPY_RE) to C8/H1/H7/M3-M5 norm artifacts at write time. Defense in depth: the prompt rule reduces exposure in the paid-LLM response; a write-time scrub is what makes leakage structurally impossible. This packet's scope was the prompt regime; the runtime scrub is a distinct, larger change.
residual_risks.note: Deliberately flagged rather than silently attempted -- this is the honest boundary of what a prompt-layer fix can deliver.

residual_risks.risk: The secret is still sent TO the provider inside <repo_content> regardless of redaction. Redaction governs what the model WRITES BACK into artifacts, not what it READS.
residual_risks.recommendation: Out of scope for F-23 as scoped (which is about excerpt exfiltration into artifacts + response context). Reducing inbound exposure means pre-scrubbing build_partition_context() input, which would corrupt the very scan C8 exists to perform. Worth an explicit program-level decision, not a silent fix.

residual_risks.risk: Over-redaction could hide real findings if a model masks aggressively (e.g. redacting env var NAMES, which are H1's intended product).
residual_risks.recommendation: Mitigated in the rule text: an explicit 'Never redact non-secret context' clause plus 'mask the value span only', and H1/H7 each restate that NAMES/paths/columns must not be masked. Unverified against a live model.

residual_risks.risk: load_promptset() now raises PromptSectionContractError where it previously always returned. Any caller that added a non-conforming prompt would newly fail closed.
residual_risks.recommendation: Intended (fail-closed is the point of F-31). Blast radius measured: the shipped promptset yields 0 issues, and the full 1432-test suite shows no new failure. enforce_sections=False is available for inspection tooling.

residual_risks.risk: Delimiter/redaction-token escape: a file body containing the literal '<REDACTED>' could make a genuine finding look pre-redacted.
residual_risks.recommendation: Same class as the unhandled '</repo_content>' escape R3-002 recorded. Worth folding into one escaping packet.
